slides.stem: A retailer marks up the cost of a jacket by $80\%$, then applies a $30\%$ discount to the marked-up price. The final price represents what percent change from the original cost?

slides.body: Stack the multipliers: up $80\%$ is $\times 1.80$, down $30\%$ is $\times 0.70$, and $1.80 \times 0.70 = 1.26$. That's a $26\%$ increase. Adding $+80 - 30 = 50$ feels natural, but the discount applies to the bigger marked-up number, not the original.

slides.title: Percent changes multiply
slides.body:
Convert every percent change to a multiplier and multiply them in one line: $+80\%$ is $\times 1.8$, $-30\%$ is $\times 0.7$.

Successive changes never add. The second change always acts on the number the first one created.
